Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex EV Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a question after the presentation. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:  
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex EV Inc.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 2024 marked a period of significant advancement for Apex EV Inc., as we continued to execute our strategic plan. Key achievements included resilient average selling prices holding at $53,200 blended globally with premium mix gains, disciplined raw material cost reductions through diversified sourcing and hedging, rapid charging network growth to over 112,000 ports with utilization climbing to 34%, major factory expansions like Gigafactory Nevada Phase 2 coming online ahead of schedule, targeted capex of $3.2 billion focused on high-ROI battery and capacity builds, record vehicle deliveries exceeding 550,000 units across regions, and effective mitigation of raw material volatility and supply disruptions via localization and inventory buffers. The launch of our Apex Lunar flagship SUV variant has been incredibly successful, and we are seeing a very positive impact on our brand image through strong order backlogs and market share gains in the luxury segment.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Jordan Lee:  
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. For Q3 2024, our revenue was $14.2 billion, representing a substantial 42% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin reached 26.2%, driven by increased production efficiencies, favorable product mix shifts toward premium models, and raw material cost deflation. Operating expenses totaled $3.1 billion, reflecting investments in R&D and sales expansion, while net income amounted to $1.4 billion. We are in a strong financial position with $9.2 billion in cash reserves and minimal net debt. We project revenue of $15.0 to $15.5 billion for Q4, with gross margins expanding toward 27-28% as efficiencies compound and deliveries accelerate.

Let me expand on some key drivers starting with average selling price trends by model and region, a focal point amid EV pricing pressures from China's price wars, U.S. IRA benefits, and Europe's subsidy reductions. Our disciplined pricing, premium mix shift, and cost reductions enabled us to outperform industry declines of 8-10% year-over-year. Global blended ASP landed at $53,200, down only 3% year-over-year and flat quarter-over-quarter, bolstered by a 12% rise in premium model mix to 42% of volumes and 65% attachment rates for our ApexDrive Full Self-Driving suite, adding $8,500 per vehicle. Configurator upsells hit 22% for performance packs and ultra-fast charging.

By model: Apex Spark entry-level sedan at 35% volume saw $36,800 ASP, down 7% year-over-year due to LFP competition, but our hybrid LFP-NCM structural packs maintained 18% margins; the new Spark Pro trim lifted North America ASP 5% quarter-over-quarter. Apex Glide mid-size SUV held at $49,200, up 2%, thanks to gigacasting and 800V architecture for Euro 7 compliance. Apex flagship SUV jumped 9% to $68,500 on Plaid tri-motor demand and 4680 cells for 510-mile range, gaining U.S. share versus Lucid and Rivian with 28,000-unit Lunar backlog. Apex Haul pickup rose 6% to $74,300, outperforming F-150 Lightning via 450-mile range and 40% Haul Max attachment.

Regionally: North America at 52% revenue delivered $58,900 ASP, up 5%, fueled by IRA 30D credits on 92% sales and 60% local content from Texas GigaFactory. Europe at $55,400 ASP dipped 2% from subsidy cliffs but rose 3% quarter-over-quarter with Berlin gigacasting offsetting tariffs. China at $42,100 faced 12% pressure but held 14% margins via 95% localization; Rest of World flat at $51,200 with Australia incentives boosting Haul.

Outlook: Q4 ASP at $53,500-$54,500, FY25 growth of 4-6% from 50% premium target, 20% bill-of-materials cuts via 4680 cells and unboxed processes, plus software localization in China.

Next, total vehicle deliveries: We delivered 550,000 vehicles globally in Q3, up 20% year-over-year from 458,000 and 12% quarter-over-quarter, solidifying our position as a top pure-play EV maker. By model: Apex Spark-like NovaCore equivalent at 295,000 units, up 22%; Glide SUV at 185,000, 35% growth on long-range LFP; Haul pickup at 50,000, 150% ramp; premium at 20,000 with margin gains. North America 275,000 (50%), up 25% on IRA; Europe 105,000 (19%), 8%; China 140,000 (26%), 15%; APAC/Other 30,000 (5%), 30%. Inventory at 28 days, backlog 1.2 million. Q4 guide 580,000-600,000; FY24 2.3 million.

On capex plans for FY25: $3.2 billion, up 28%, prioritized for 25%+ IRR projects funded by cash flow and low-cost debt. 45% or $1.44 billion to capacity: $900 million Reno Phase 2 for 40 GWh prismatic 46-series cells at $65/kWh target; $400 million South Carolina plant for IRA credits; Europe Hungary JV. 30% or $960 million R&D: solid-state pilots for 700 Wh/kg, NovaPilot Level 3 autonomy, SDV. 20% supply chain resilience: U.S. pCAM, graphite refinery. 5% charging buildout. Capex intensity to fall to 8% by 2027 on volume growth.

Finally, raw material costs and disruptions impacted COGS up 18% year-over-year, compressing margins 250 bps to 22.4% initially, from lithium peaks at $82,000/ton, nickel 60% spikes, graphite 40% rises. But Q3 averages stabilized—lithium $65,000 flat—with 60% hedged offtakes from Ganfeng/Piedmont. Disruptions deferred 12,000 units via semis, Red Sea freight +25%, cell delays; countered by 40% LFP shift cutting nickel 60%, $500 million Georgia LFP giga, inventory to 45 days. Tailwinds ahead: lithium to $40-45k, margins to 25%+ Q4.

Next, Maria Gonzalez will share updates on our manufacturing operations.

Maria Gonzalez:  
Thank you, Jordan. We have made significant investments in our manufacturing facilities to enhance capacity and improve efficiency. Our efforts have resulted in record production volumes and reduced manufacturing costs. We've allocated $4.2 billion in capex this year, 65% to expansions like Gigafactory Nevada Phase 2 now at 50 GWh doubling U.S. output for 4680 structural cells with 16% higher density, supporting 500,000 Aerion SUV units and $1.1 billion IRA incentives. Europe Hungary gigafactory at 40 GWh by 2026 for LFP compliance; China Shanghai +30 GWh sodium-ion; Thailand assembly for ASEAN.

Efficiency gains drove 320 bps gross margin to 28.4%: Siemens MindSphere IIoT to 94% OEE, 1,200 robots/10k associates, 37% less downtime, 98.5% battery yield. Verticalization cut kWh costs 14% to $68; renewables 85%, 24% labor productivity to 1.2 vehicles/associate/shift, 18x inventory turns, 16.2% EBITDA. Targeting $95/kWh by 2026 for sub-$30k models.

After me, we will hear from Dr. Elena Vasquez regarding our technological advancements.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:  
Thank you. Our R&D team continues to push the boundaries of innovation in battery technology, autonomous driving, and connectivity. We are committed to developing cutting-edge solutions that will shape the future of mobility. A prime example is our ApexCharge network, expanded 45% year-over-year to 112,000 ports across 18,000 sites, with Q3 adding 9,500 including 4,200 250kW DC fast chargers. North America 65,000 ports (58%), Europe 32,000 up 55% with 1MW V2G hubs for AFIR mandates, China 10,000 via State Grid JV, India pilots.

Utilization hit 34% global average, up 28% year-over-year, generating $285 million revenue at $2,540 ARPU/port; peaks 68% via dynamic pricing. Roaming with Electrify/IONITY/Tesla NACS added 40% non-Apex sessions; AI load balancing cut waits 22%, V2G arbitrage at $0.18/kWh premiums, 500kW Trinity chargers upcoming. FY24 capex $1.4-1.6 billion for 400kW stalls; raised revenue guide $1.1-1.3 billion, 50% CAGR to 2027. This builds our moat, free charging for Prime subs at 65% uptake, <5% range anxiety.

Following me, Raj Patel will provide insights into our supply chain management.

Raj Patel:  
Thank you. We have implemented robust supply chain strategies to mitigate risks and ensure the reliable flow of materials. Our focus on diversification and strategic partnerships has strengthened our supply chain resilience. Raw materials are 42% of COGS for our platforms, down from 48%, with Q3 17% year-over-year per-vehicle reduction or $1,200 savings on high-volume lines. Lithium 35% drop to $14,500/ton aided; FY deflation 15-18% for 28% EBITDA.

Diversified: Lithium 22% spend, 70% locked 2024-2026 from Albemarle/SQM at $12-15k floors; nickel/cobalt down 25% via 40% LFP from BYD at $85/kWh, low-cobalt NMC, 95% recycling. Anodes graphite $8,500/ton; copper 60% Codelco/Freeport for IRA $150 million credits. North America 55% sourcing, Europe 30% for CRMA/CBAM, APAC 15%. Vertical: $2.5 billion Piedmont JV Tennessee hydroxide H2 2025; $300 million Redwood recycling for 20 GWh; sodium-ion pilots. Solid-state with QuantumScape, DLE with Lilac. Q4 another 8-10% lower; 80% contracted, multi-year with LG.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:  
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Our first question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Analyst 1:  
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On ASP, with China pressures and potential U.S. tariffs, how confident are you in the $53,500-$54,500 Q4 guide and FY25 growth?

Alex Rivera:  
Great question, Mike. We're highly confident given our 320,000-unit backlog weighted 40% to high-ASP models like Haul and Lunar, premium mix targeting 50%, and 20% BoM cuts from 4680 and unboxed processes. China rebates and 35% FSD localization offset pricing; NA IRA fortress intact. We'll detail at Investor Day.

Operator:  
Our next question from Lisa Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Analyst 2:  
Jordan, margins expanded nicely—can you walk through the puts and takes for Q4 guidance, especially capex impact?

Jordan Lee:  
Sure, Lisa. Key puts: modest raw mat residuals and Q4 incentive normalization; takes: 28.4% from efficiencies, LFP shift, 34% charging utilization revenue. Capex $3.2 billion disciplined at 15% revenue but high-ROI, cash flow covers $1.8 billion. EBITDA to 18% Q4, ROIC 25%+.

Operator:  
Next from David Kim with JPMorgan.

Analyst 3:  
Maria, impressive Nevada ramp—any bottlenecks in Hungary or Thailand, and how does OEE trend into FY25?

Maria Gonzalez:  
David, Nevada ahead on 4680; Hungary groundbreaking smooth for 40 GWh LFP, 80% local recycled for regs. Thailand ASEAN exports via FTAs. OEE 94% holds with AI predictive maintenance; targeting 1.2 veh/associate, 30%+ ROIC scaling to 2.5 million units FY27.

Operator:  
From Sarah Lopez with Barclays.

Analyst 4:  
Elena, charging utilization strong—thoughts on grid risks in Europe and V2G monetization scale?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:  
Sarah, 500 MWh solar+battery pilots mitigate EU grid for 10-15% sites; NEVI funds 20,000 U.S. ports. V2G ApexFlow with 500 R2 trucks yields 15% arbitrage; Prime 65% uptake, 2.8 TWh dispensed up 55%. 50% revenue CAGR locked.

Operator:  
From Tom Reilly with Credit Suisse.

Analyst 5:  
Raj, lithium hedges great—what's the exposure to nickel tightness or copper deficits?

Raj Patel:  
Tom, nickel low via LFP 40% mix, Indonesia HPAL ramps hedged 75%; copper IEA 500kt deficit covered by Codelco dual-source, IRA credits. 65 days inventory optimal; dynamic clauses with CATL/LG share tailwinds. Multi-year 80% locked.

Sarah Johnson:  
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Operator:  
Our final question from Emma Wong with Deutsche Bank.

Analyst 6:  
Alex, holistically, with deliveries accelerating and capex scaling, how do you see free cash flow inflection and competitive positioning versus Tesla/BYD?

Alex Rivera:  
Emma, FCF positive inflection H1 2025 as utilization >30% per charging site, efficiencies compound, backlog converts. Versus Tesla, our 4680/LFP blend and ApexDrive close gaps; BYD, premium NA/EU moat plus China JV volumes. $1.2 trillion market by 2030 ours to capture at 30% margins.

Operator:  
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for electric vehicles and deliver strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Sarah Johnson:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Apex EV Inc. Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
